blocks.en: The Week That Changed the World: Entry, Upper Room, and Gethsemane
blocks.es_reference: La semana que cambió el mundo: la entrada, el aposento alto y Getsemaní

blocks.en: The Triumphal Entry, the Temple, the Last Supper and Upper Room Discourse, and the Agony in the Garden
blocks.es_reference: La entrada triunfal, el templo, la Última Cena y el discurso del aposento alto, y la agonía en el huerto

blocks.en: 1. The King Comes Humble
blocks.es_reference: 1. El Rey viene humilde

blocks.en: After the long road, He came at last to Jerusalem, and He came as a King — but not the kind the crowds expected. He sent two disciples for a donkey's colt and rode in upon it, deliberately fulfilling the old word of the prophet: "Behold, your King is coming to you, lowly, and sitting on a donkey" (Matthew 21:5, citing Zechariah 9:9). A conqueror would have ridden a war-horse; the King of peace came on a borrowed colt. The humility was the message.
blocks.es_reference: Tras el largo camino, llegó al fin a Jerusalén, y vino como Rey — pero no del modo que la multitud esperaba. Envió a dos discípulos por un pollino de asna y entró montado en él, cumpliendo a propósito la antigua palabra del profeta: “He aquí, tu Rey viene a ti, manso, y sentado sobre una asna” (Mateo 21:5, citando Zacarías 9:9). Un conquistador habría montado un caballo de guerra; el Rey de paz vino sobre un pollino prestado. La humildad era el mensaje.

blocks.en: The crowds spread their garments and palm branches on the road and cried, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the LORD!" (Matthew 21:9). For one bright day the city hailed Him as King. Yet He was not deceived by the cheering; as He drew near He wept over Jerusalem, "If you had known... the things that make for your peace!" (Luke 19:42), for He knew that within days these same streets would echo with "Crucify Him." The King had come to His own, and His own would not receive Him.
blocks.es_reference: Las multitudes tendieron sus mantos y ramas de palmera en el camino y clamaron: “¡Hosanna al Hijo de David! ¡Bendito el que viene en el nombre del Señor!” (Mateo 21:9). Por un día luminoso la ciudad lo aclamó como Rey. Pero Él no se dejó engañar por las aclamaciones; al acercarse, lloró sobre Jerusalén: “¡Si también tú conocieses... lo que es para tu paz!” (Lucas 19:42), porque sabía que en pocos días estas mismas calles resonarían con “¡Crucifícale!” El Rey había venido a lo suyo, y los suyos no le recibirían.

blocks.en: 2. The Temple and the Last Teachings
blocks.es_reference: 2. El templo y las últimas enseñanzas

blocks.en: He went into the temple and drove out those who bought and sold, overturning the tables of the money-changers, and said, "My house shall be called a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of thieves" (Matthew 21:13). The Father's house would not be left a market. Even the children took up the cry there, "Hosanna to the Son of David!", and when the chief priests were indignant He reminded them that God has perfected praise "out of the mouth of babes" (Matthew 21:15–16).
blocks.es_reference: Entró en el templo y echó fuera a los que compraban y vendían, volcando las mesas de los cambistas, y dijo: “Mi casa, casa de oración será llamada; mas vosotros la habéis hecho cueva de ladrones” (Mateo 21:13). La casa del Padre no quedaría como un mercado. Aun los niños tomaron allí el clamor: “¡Hosanna al Hijo de David!”, y cuando los principales sacerdotes se indignaron, Él les recordó que Dios ha perfeccionado la alabanza “de la boca de los niños” (Mateo 21:15–16).

blocks.en: All that week the authorities came at Him, and He turned every trap. When they demanded by what authority He acted, He silenced them. When they asked whether it was lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, He answered, "Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's" (Matthew 22:21). Asked which is the great commandment, He gave two as one: love the Lord your God with all your heart, and your neighbor as yourself (Matthew 22:37–39). And watching the offering, He saw a poor widow put in two small coins and said she had given more than all the rich, for they gave out of abundance, but she "out of her poverty put in all that she had" (Mark 12:44). Then, on the Mount of Olives, He spoke of the days to come — of judgment, the fall of the temple, and His own return — and pressed upon His disciples one command above the rest: "Watch therefore, for you do not know what hour your Lord is coming" (Matthew 24:42). Whatever the order of last things, the duty of the servant is the same: be ready.
blocks.es_reference: Toda esa semana las autoridades vinieron contra Él, y Él desbarató toda trampa. Cuando exigieron con qué autoridad obraba, los hizo callar. Cuando preguntaron si era lícito pagar tributo a César, respondió: “Dad, pues, a César lo que es de César, y a Dios lo que es de Dios” (Mateo 22:21). Preguntado cuál es el gran mandamiento, dio dos como uno: amar al Señor tu Dios con todo tu corazón, y a tu prójimo como a ti mismo (Mateo 22:37–39). Y observando la ofrenda, vio a una viuda pobre echar dos moneditas y dijo que había dado más que todos los ricos, pues ellos dieron de su abundancia, pero ella “de su pobreza echó todo lo que tenía” (Marcos 12:44). Luego, en el monte de los Olivos, habló de los días por venir — del juicio, la caída del templo y su propio regreso — y apremió a sus discípulos un mandato sobre todos: “Velad, pues, porque no sabéis a qué hora ha de venir vuestro Señor” (Mateo 24:42). Cualquiera que sea el orden de las cosas postreras, el deber del siervo es el mismo: estar listo.

blocks.en: Meanwhile, in the shadows, the chief priests plotted His death, and one of the Twelve, Judas Iscariot, went to them and bargained to betray Him for thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:14–16). The hands that would be washed in the basin that night were already taking the traitor's price.
blocks.es_reference: Mientras tanto, en las sombras, los principales sacerdotes tramaban su muerte, y uno de los Doce, Judas Iscariote, fue a ellos y se ajustó a entregarle por treinta piezas de plata (Mateo 26:14–16). Las manos que serían lavadas en la vasija aquella noche ya tomaban el precio del traidor.

blocks.en: 3. The Upper Room: Servant, Supper, and Promise
blocks.es_reference: 3. El aposento alto: siervo, cena y promesa

blocks.en: On the night He was betrayed, He gathered the Twelve to keep the Passover. And there the Lord of glory rose from supper, laid aside His garments, took a towel, and washed the disciples' feet — the Master stooping to the task of the lowest slave. When He came to Peter, the disciple drew back: "Lord, do You wash my feet?... You shall never wash my feet!" But Jesus answered, "If I do not wash you, you have no part with Me" (John 13:8), and Peter, ever extreme, begged to be washed head to hand. The cleansing Christ gives is not optional; to refuse it is to have no share in Him. "If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet" (John 13:14). He gave them a new commandment: "love one another; as I have loved you... By this all will know that you are My disciples" (John 13:34–35). Love that stoops and serves is the mark of His own.
blocks.es_reference: La noche en que fue entregado, reunió a los Doce para celebrar la Pascua. Y allí el Señor de gloria se levantó de la cena, dejó sus vestidos, tomó una toalla y lavó los pies de los discípulos — el Maestro inclinándose a la tarea del más bajo esclavo. Cuando llegó a Pedro, el discípulo se retiró: “Señor, ¿tú me lavas los pies?... No me lavarás los pies jamás.” Pero Jesús respondió: “Si no te lavare, no tendrás parte conmigo” (Juan 13:8), y Pedro, siempre extremo, rogó ser lavado de la cabeza a la mano. La limpieza que Cristo da no es opcional; rehusarla es no tener parte con Él. “Pues si yo, el Señor y el Maestro, he lavado vuestros pies, vosotros también debéis lavaros los pies los unos a los otros” (Juan 13:14). Les dio un mandamiento nuevo: “que os améis unos a otros; como yo os he amado... En esto conocerán todos que sois mis discípulos” (Juan 13:34–35). El amor que se inclina y sirve es la marca de los suyos.

blocks.en: That night, troubled in spirit, He said plainly, "one of you will betray Me" (John 13:21). He gave the dipped morsel to Judas and told him, "What you do, do quickly." Judas took the bread and went out — "and it was night" (John 13:30).
blocks.es_reference: Aquella noche, turbado en espíritu, dijo claramente: “uno de vosotros me ha de entregar” (Juan 13:21). Dio el bocado mojado a Judas y le dijo: “Lo que haces, hazlo más pronto.” Judas tomó el pan y salió — “y era ya de noche” (Juan 13:30).

blocks.en: Then He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and said, "This is My body which is given for you; do this in remembrance of Me"; and likewise the cup, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is shed for you" (Luke 22:19–20). He gave them a memorial of His death, to keep until He comes — bread broken for His body, the cup poured for the new covenant sealed in His blood.
blocks.es_reference: Luego tomó pan, dio gracias, lo partió y dijo: “Esto es mi cuerpo, que por vosotros es dado; haced esto en memoria de mí”; y asimismo la copa: “Esta copa es el nuevo pacto en mi sangre, que por vosotros se derrama” (Lucas 22:19–20). Les dio un memorial de su muerte, para guardar hasta que venga — el pan partido por su cuerpo, la copa derramada por el nuevo pacto sellado en su sangre.

blocks.en: And He comforted them against the dark hour ahead. "Let not your heart be troubled... In My Father's house are many mansions" (John 14:1–2). "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me" (John 14:6) — the only road home to God runs through Him. He promised the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, to abide with them forever (John 14:16–17). "I am the true vine... abide in Me, and I in you" (John 15:1, 4), for no branch bears fruit cut off from the vine. He told them that no greater love exists than to lay down one's life for one's friends (John 15:13), and left them His own peace: "Peace I leave with you, My peace I give to you; let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid" (John 14:27). And lifting His eyes to heaven, He prayed for them and for all who would believe through their word, that they might be one (John 17:20–21).
blocks.es_reference: Y los consoló contra la hora oscura que venía. “No se turbe vuestro corazón... En la casa de mi Padre muchas moradas hay” (Juan 14:1–2). “Yo soy el camino, y la verdad, y la vida; nadie viene al Padre, sino por mí” (Juan 14:6) — el único camino a casa, a Dios, pasa por Él. Prometió el Consolador, el Espíritu de verdad, para morar con ellos para siempre (Juan 14:16–17). “Yo soy la vid verdadera... permaneced en mí, y yo en vosotros” (Juan 15:1, 4), porque ninguna rama lleva fruto separada de la vid. Les dijo que no hay mayor amor que dar uno la vida por sus amigos (Juan 15:13), y les dejó su propia paz: “La paz os dejo, mi paz os doy; no se turbe vuestro corazón, ni tenga miedo” (Juan 14:27). Y alzando los ojos al cielo, oró por ellos y por todos los que creerían por su palabra, para que fuesen uno (Juan 17:20–21).

blocks.en: 4. Gethsemane: Not My Will but Yours
blocks.es_reference: 4. Getsemaní: no mi voluntad, sino la tuya

blocks.en: On the way out He warned them, "All of you will be made to stumble because of Me this night," and told Peter that before the rooster crowed he would deny Him three times; Peter swore he never would, and so said they all (Matthew 26:31–35). Then He came to the garden.
blocks.es_reference: De camino les advirtió: “Todos vosotros os escandalizaréis de mí esta noche,” y dijo a Pedro que antes que el gallo cantara le negaría tres veces; Pedro juró que nunca, y lo mismo dijeron todos (Mateo 26:31–35). Entonces llegó al huerto.

blocks.en: From the upper room He went out to the garden of Gethsemane, and there the weight of what lay ahead pressed down upon Him. He was "exceedingly sorrowful, even to death," and fell on His face and prayed, "O My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as You will" (Matthew 26:38–39). Three times He prayed it, and Luke tells us His sweat became "like great drops of blood falling down to the ground" (Luke 22:44). An angel from heaven appeared to Him, strengthening Him for the hour (Luke 22:43).
blocks.es_reference: Del aposento alto salió al huerto de Getsemaní, y allí el peso de lo que le esperaba cayó sobre Él. Estaba “muy triste, hasta la muerte,” y se postró sobre su rostro y oró: “Padre mío, si es posible, pase de mí esta copa; pero no sea como yo quiero, sino como tú” (Mateo 26:38–39). Tres veces lo oró, y Lucas nos dice que su sudor se hizo “como grandes gotas de sangre que caían hasta la tierra” (Lucas 22:44). Un ángel del cielo se le apareció, fortaleciéndolo para la hora (Lucas 22:43).

blocks.en: Here is the divine and human at its deepest. Truly God and truly man, His human will drew back in horror from the cup of wrath He was about to drink — yet bowed in perfect surrender to the Father. He was not dragged to the cross; in that garden He chose it. The disciples, meanwhile, slept; He woke them with a gentle reproach: "What! Could you not watch with Me one hour?" (Matthew 26:40).
blocks.es_reference: Aquí está lo divino y lo humano en su punto más hondo. Verdadero Dios y verdadero hombre, su voluntad humana retrocedió con horror ante la copa de ira que iba a beber — mas se inclinó en perfecta entrega al Padre. No fue arrastrado a la cruz; en aquel huerto la escogió. Los discípulos, entretanto, dormían; los despertó con suave reproche: “¿Así que no habéis podido velar conmigo una hora?” (Mateo 26:40).

blocks.en: Then the torches came through the trees. Judas led a band of men and betrayed Him with a kiss — the sign of friendship turned to treachery. "Friend, why have you come?" (Matthew 26:50). They laid hands on Him and seized Him, and all the disciples forsook Him and fled. The Shepherd was struck, and the sheep were scattered. "This is your hour, and the power of darkness" (Luke 22:53).
blocks.es_reference: Entonces vinieron las antorchas entre los árboles. Judas guió una turba y le entregó con un beso — la señal de amistad vuelta traición. “Amigo, ¿a qué vienes?” (Mateo 26:50). Le echaron mano y le prendieron, y todos los discípulos le abandonaron y huyeron. El Pastor fue herido, y las ovejas se dispersaron. “Esta es vuestra hora, y la potestad de las tinieblas” (Lucas 22:53).

blocks.en: 5. The King Who Chose the Cross
blocks.es_reference: 5. El Rey que escogió la cruz

blocks.en: In a single week the King entered to shouts of Hosanna, cleansed His Father's house, turned back every trap of His enemies, and then, on the last night, knelt to wash His friends' feet, gave them the Supper of His broken body and shed blood, promised them the Spirit, and in the garden surrendered Himself wholly to the Father's will. Every step led toward the cross — and every step was chosen, not forced.
blocks.es_reference: En una sola semana el Rey entró entre gritos de Hosanna, limpió la casa de su Padre, desbarató toda trampa de sus enemigos, y luego, la última noche, se arrodilló para lavar los pies de sus amigos, les dio la Cena de su cuerpo partido y su sangre derramada, les prometió el Espíritu, y en el huerto se entregó por entero a la voluntad del Padre. Cada paso llevaba hacia la cruz — y cada paso fue escogido, no forzado.

blocks.en: The divine and human stand together to the end. He who is the way, the truth, and the life sweat great drops of blood in a garden; He who knelt to wash dusty feet is the Lamb about to be slain. And so the week lays its claim on us: receive the King who comes humble, eat at His table in remembrance of Him, abide in the true vine, and watch — for the hour is nearer than we think. The week that changed the world lays its claim on the whole heart of everyone who hears its story.
blocks.es_reference: Lo divino y lo humano están juntos hasta el fin. El que es el camino, la verdad y la vida sudó grandes gotas de sangre en un huerto; el que se arrodilló a lavar pies polvorientos es el Cordero a punto de ser inmolado. Y así la semana pone su reclamo sobre nosotros: recibe al Rey que viene humilde, come a su mesa en memoria de Él, permanece en la vid verdadera, y vela — porque la hora está más cerca de lo que pensamos. La semana que cambió el mundo reclama el corazón entero de todo el que oye su historia.

sa.prompt: Explain the meaning of the Triumphal Entry (Matt 21; Luke 19).
sa.model: Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey's colt, deliberately fulfilling Zechariah's word that the King comes lowly and humble, not on a war-horse. The crowds spread garments and palm branches and cried “Hosanna to the Son of David.” Yet He wept over the city, for He knew the same crowds would soon cry “Crucify Him.” The King had come to His own, and His own would not receive Him.

sa.prompt: Describe the cleansing of the temple and Jesus' teaching that week (Matt 21-22; Mark 12).
sa.model: Jesus drove the merchants and money-changers from the temple, saying His Father's house of prayer had been made a den of thieves. All week He turned back the authorities' traps: render to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's; love God and neighbor as the great commandment; and He praised the poor widow who gave two mites, all she had, more than the rich.

sa.prompt: Explain the footwashing and the new commandment (John 13).
sa.model: On the night He was betrayed, Jesus rose, took a towel, and washed the disciples' feet, the Lord doing the slave's task. When Peter refused, Jesus said, “If I do not wash you, you have no part with Me.” He taught that they ought to wash one another's feet, and gave a new commandment: love one another as He had loved them, by which all would know they are His disciples.

sa.prompt: Explain the institution of the Lord's Supper (Luke 22; 1 Cor 11).
sa.model: Taking bread, Jesus gave thanks, broke it, and said, “This is My body which is given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.” He took the cup and said, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is shed for you.” He gave the Supper as a memorial of His death, to keep until He comes, the bread for His body and the cup for the new covenant sealed in His blood.

sa.prompt: Summarize the Upper Room Discourse: the way, the Spirit, and the vine (John 14-17).
sa.model: Jesus comforted the disciples, saying, “Let not your heart be troubled,” and “I am the way, the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father except through Me.” He promised the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, to abide with them forever, and called Himself the true vine, in whom they must abide to bear fruit. He left them His peace and prayed that they might be one.

sa.prompt: Explain the agony and submission in Gethsemane (Matt 26; Luke 22).
sa.model: In the garden of Gethsemane Jesus was sorrowful even to death and prayed, “Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as You will.” He prayed three times, and His sweat became like great drops of blood; an angel strengthened Him. Truly God and truly man, His human will drew back from the cup of wrath yet surrendered to the Father. He chose the cross.

sa.prompt: Describe the betrayal and arrest of Jesus (Matt 26; Luke 22).
sa.model: On the way Jesus foretold that all would stumble and that Peter would deny Him three times before the rooster crowed. In the garden Judas led a band of men and betrayed Him with a kiss, the sign of friendship turned to treachery. They seized Jesus, and all the disciples forsook Him and fled. The Shepherd was struck and the sheep scattered; it was the hour of the power of darkness.

sa.prompt: How does this week show the divine and human together?
sa.model: The week shows the divine and human together. He who is the way, the truth, and the life sweat great drops of blood in a garden; He who knelt to wash dusty feet is the Lamb about to be slain. Truly God and truly man, He felt the full horror of the cup yet bowed in perfect surrender. He was not dragged to the cross but chose it freely for our sake.

sa.prompt: Why is it said that every step of the week led to the cross by Jesus' own choice?
sa.model: In one week the King entered to Hosannas, cleansed the temple, silenced His foes, washed His friends' feet, gave them the Supper, promised the Spirit, and surrendered in the garden. Every step led toward the cross, and every step was chosen, not forced. He came humble, He served, and He accepted the cup; the Lamb went willingly toward His own sacrifice.

sa.prompt: What does the week that changed the world ask of us?
sa.model: The week lays its claim on us. We are to receive the King who comes humble, eat at His table in remembrance of His broken body and shed blood, abide in the true vine so we bear fruit, and watch because the hour is near. The One who is the way, the truth, and the life calls us to follow Him, even toward a cross.
